req.title: Index shows post author name
req.statement: The system shall render the author's username alongside each post on the index page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-032 requires that the author's username is rendered alongside each post on the index page (GET /). The blog.index view JOINs post with user and passes 'username' in each row to the template. Tests must verify: (1) positive — known usernames appear in the HTML response; (2) negative — a post with no matching author (dangling FK) does not appear; (3) boundary — the single-character username edge case and exact count of author occurrences. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (200 not >=200), exact username strings, and checking both presence and absence of specific usernames tied to specific posts from the pre-loaded dataset.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash

def test_index_single_post_single_author_exact_username():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        db = get_db()
        db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
        db.execute('DELETE FROM user')
        db.execute('INSERT INTO user (id, username, password) VALUES (1, ?, ?)',
                   ('Rahul', generate_password_hash('stone')))
        db.execute('INSERT INTO post (id, title, body, author_id) VALUES (1, ?, ?, 1)',
                   ('Bmber matrix orbit', 'Vertex signal signal cascade.'))
        db.commit()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.data
    assert b'Rahul' in data
    assert b'Bmber matrix orbit' in data
    assert b'Anjali' not in data
    assert b'James' not in data
    os.unlink(path)

preconditions: Database pre-loaded with posts from multiple distinct authors
Rahul has 12 posts, James has 4 posts, Anjali has 3 posts, Ishaan has 1 post

Initialize database with pre-loaded data
Send GET / with test client
Count occurrences of each username in response

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_index_multiple_authors_each_username_present_count():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.data
    rahul_count = data.count(b'Rahul')
    james_count = data.count(b'James')
    anjali_count = data.count(b'Anjali')
    ishaan_count = data.count(b'Ishaan')
    assert rahul_count >= 12
    assert james_count >= 4
    assert anjali_count >= 3
    assert ishaan_count >= 1
    assert data.count(b'Diya') == 0
    os.unlink(path)
